A1.justification: The retitled PDFs describe the same rank-based oversmoothing study. Both provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–G, allowing revised and relocated material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendices D–G report original GCN/GAT classification experiments, metric–accuracy correlations and synthetic-network results.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendices D–G retain these original experimental results, including trained-network comparisons and synthetic simulations.

M1.justification: The numerical/effective-rank measures and GCN/GAT procedures remain unchanged. Revised theoretical assumptions and proposed future architectural applications do not introduce an implemented method component.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same eight real-world node-classification datasets, including Roman Empire in Appendix E, and retain the same Barabasi–Albert synthetic graph and toy scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparisons: Erank and NumRank against standard and normalized EDir/EProj and MAD. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain default dataset splits, hidden dimension 32, eight depths spanning 2–24 layers, NAdam with learning rate 0.01, and last-hidden-layer measurements. Synthetic settings, component configurations and correlation calculations also match.

E4.justification: The toy outlier scenarios, synthetic weight-size/activation analysis, architectural-component comparisons and Appendix G case plots are retained without new empirical ablations or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Both report averaging results over 10 separately trained GNNs. There are no changes to seed disclosure, uncertainty displays, confidence intervals or statistical testing.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–7 and the plotted experimental evidence match. For example, Table 1 retains average correlations of 0.9103 for Erank and 0.8374 for NumRank; Table 2 retains identical convergence outcomes.

T1.justification: v4 adds energy-equivalence Lemma A.1 and three convergence regimes in Appendix A.6, including weak-ergodic Theorem A.5. It reorganizes v3's uniformly contractive nonlinear result into Lemma 5.2 and conditional Theorem 5.3, removing the old contractivity definition/example. The activation-eigenvector proposition is retained as Proposition A.6.

C1.justification: The central claim favoring rank metrics remains. v4 removes v3's explicit priority claim for the first nonlinear proof without weight-magnitude bounds and instead claims a gap in explicit rank-metric evaluation. Its abstract drops the nonnegative-weight qualification, although the introduction retains that restriction.

C2.justification: v4 distinguishes aggregation-driven and activation-driven contraction, strengthens the attribution of energy decay to small initialization, and suggests architectural applications of rank metrics in Section 7. Appendix B's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain the same, including optimizer settings, synthetic weight distributions, DropEdge probability and the residual-update formula. No new hardware, training-time or code/data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v4 adds five references, including Nussbaum (1990), Jin and Zhu (2024), and Arnaiz-Rodriguez and Errica (2025). It explicitly distinguishes its metric evaluation from the rank-collapse ideas of already-cited Guo et al. and Roth and Liebig; most research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, and the abstract and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten to foreground metric evaluation. The nonlinear theory is reorganized across the main text and appendix, the activation-eigenvector proposition is relocated, and the conclusion is expanded.

P2.justification: The new template changes the author block, heading typography and page rules, with adjusted display sizing, spacing and caption wrapping. Both figures and all seven tables are retained with the same experimental content.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies research positioning and expands the explanation of rank-collapse mechanisms. However, Equation (45) does not constrain pi(X) to the rank-one set Pi required by the new Theorem A.5 proof. This definition/proof mismatch limits confidence in the expanded theory. With empirical evidence unchanged, the explanatory gains and theoretical reliability concerns leave the net quality direction uncertain.
